events.title: Pope Pius V excommunicates Elizabeth I
events.description: Pope Pius V issued the papal bull Regnans in Excelsis, declaring Queen Elizabeth I a heretic and excommunicating her and her followers in the Church of England.
events.significance: The decree deepened the divide between England and Rome. It also put English Catholics in a painful position, since they were pushed to choose between loyalty to the Pope and loyalty to the Crown.

events.title: Samuel Colt patents the revolver
events.description: American inventor Samuel Colt received a US patent for a 'revolving gun', a firearm with a rotating cylinder that let a shooter fire several rounds without reloading.
events.significance: The Colt revolver changed personal firearms and became a symbol of the American frontier. It also helped make Colt a pioneer of mass production.

events.title: Cassius Clay becomes heavyweight champion
events.description: Cassius Clay, who soon took the name Muhammad Ali, beat Sonny Liston in Miami Beach when Liston failed to come out for the seventh round. The win made Clay world heavyweight champion.
events.significance: It was the start of the career of one of the most famous athletes of the 20th century. Ali became a global figure in sport, civil rights and culture.

events.title: Corazon Aquino sworn in as President of the Philippines
events.description: Corazon Aquino took the oath of office as the 11th President of the Philippines. This followed the People Power Revolution, which forced Ferdinand Marcos from power.
events.significance: Her inauguration ended two decades of dictatorship and restored democracy in the Philippines. It also inspired nonviolent protest movements around the world.

events.title: The Warsaw Pact is declared disbanded
events.description: The Soviet-led military alliance of Eastern Bloc nations was formally declared dissolved, ending a coalition that had stood opposite NATO throughout the Cold War.
events.significance: The end of the Warsaw Pact was one of the clearest signs that the Cold War was over. It came months before the Soviet Union itself dissolved.
